function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have a function that will return *all* node‑level details for a fabric.  
The only telemetry function available here is `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get`, which requires you to specify a particular node (by its numeric `nodeId`) and a pod (`podId`).  

If you already know the node’s numeric ID (or if you can look it up from your inventory), you can call:

```json
{
  "fabricName": "test-de",
  "nodeId": <NODE_ID>,
  "podId": <POD_ID>,
  "interfaceType": "interfaces",   // or "status", "statistics", "errors"
  "infoType": "interfaces"         // choose the data you need
}
```

That will give you the requested interface information for that node.

If you’re looking for a way to discover the node IDs or other high‑level node attributes (e.g., hostname, role, etc.) for all nodes in “test‑de”, you’ll need to query your device inventory or use another API endpoint that lists nodes. Once you have the node ID(s) you can then use the function above to drill down into interface details.
